plan:
FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN — "How does QuaRot's end-to-end 4-bit quantization affect the prefill and decoding performance of LLaMa-2 models?" (design-only; to be executed on a target GPU machine)

(a) RATIONALE
QuaRot (ICLR 2025) claims that rotating weights/activations with online Hadamards removes outliers so 4-bit weight+activation (+4-bit KV cache) quantization incurs negligible accuracy loss, while the smaller memory footprint and integer kernels accelerate inference. The question has two axes that must be separated:
- Prefill vs decoding: prefill is compute-bound (long prompt matmuls, growing KV cache) while decoding is memory/bandwidth-bound (cache reads, single-token steps). A 4-bit method can change them in opposite directions, so aggregate "speedup" is uninformative; we measure each phase independently.
- Speed vs quality: "performance" can mean throughput/latency or accuracy. We treat BOTH as response variables and additionally include an RTN-without-rotation ablation so we can attribute any quality loss to the quantization itself vs to the missing rotation — this is what lets us conclude whether QuaRot's 4-bit is a "pure speed boost" or a "speed/accuracy tradeoff".

(b) CONTROLS / BASELINES & CONTINGENCY SCOPE
Models: meta-llama/Llama-2-{7b,13b,70b}-hf (HF gated).
Configs per model (all share the identical prompt set, seeds, and quantized-checkpoint pipeline):
  C0 FP16 (or BF16 on H100) original — quality upper bound & speed reference. [control]
  C1 QuaRot W4A4 (online rotation, KQ rotation, 4-bit KV) — treatment. [main]
  C2 RTN W4A4 WITHOUT rotation (same 4-bit bitwidths/group size, no Hadamard) — ablation isolating rotation's contribution. [control]
  C3/C4 GPTQ W4A4 and AWQ W4A4 — alternative-method comparators (secondary; drop if budget-bound).
Contingency if 70B exceeds 80GB VRAM or budget: Tier A = full grid on 7B+13B; Tier B = add 70B only after Tier A, restricted to C0/C1/C2 at batch∈{1,8} and prompt lengths {128,512,1024}, plus a GPU-memory-footprint measurement for 70B instead of the full throughput grid. If VRAM is insufficient even for 7B inference at 4-bit, record a hard blocker (see (e)).

(c) MEASUREMENT PROTOCOL (concrete)
Environment & hygiene: 1× H100-80GB (A100-80GB acceptable), GPU exclusively reserved; pin clocks via `nvidia-smi -lgc <min,max>` (fixed base clocks); if clock pinning unavailable (cloud), record the observed clocks and treat drift as noise by interleaving. Same driver/CUDA/torch versions recorded in a pinned `requirements.lock`; build QuaRot CUDA kernels in the repo's pinned Docker image to guarantee toolchain match. Fix `torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32` and CUDA-graph enablement identically across conditions (report both settings if time permits, since graph capture changes TTFT).
Workload grid (per model, per config):
  Prompt lengths L ∈ {128, 512, 1024, 2048} tokens; fixed decode length D = 128 tokens; batch sizes B ∈ {1, 8, 32} (B=32 only on 7B/13B, and on 70B only if it fits Tier B). Same prompt text and same seed across all configs for paired comparison.
Instrumentation — two levels, both run:
  (L1) Application level via QuaRot's pinned vLLM fork: `benchmark_latency.py` for TTFT and end-to-end latency per request; parse server-side logs for TTFT and generated tokens/s; `benchmark_throughput.py` for pooled prefill/decode throughput at B≥8. Prefix caching disabled so TTFT reflects cold prefill.
  (L2) Phase-pure kernel level on the same quantized checkpoint: (i) timed single forward pass over the full prompt (prefill phase), (ii) timed autoregressive loop generating D tokens with cached KV (decode phase), per-token timing. This decouples phase statistics from vLLM scheduler effects and is the primary TTFT/prefill-tok/s/decode-tok/s source where the two disagree.
Warmup & protocol order: 2 warmup runs per condition (primes CUDA context/fused kernels); conditions randomized per model; repeat blocks interleaved to counter thermal drift; n=5 repeats per (config, L, B) for latency/throughput (n=3 minimum if budget forces, recorded as such); report all individual values in the artifact. Same random seeds for generation and for eval-set sampling. Disable speculative decoding and any sampling-time quantization for the timing runs (greedy, batch-compatible decoding).

(d) ANALYSIS PLAN
Matrix: rows = (config × model size × prompt length); primary columns = TTFT (ms), prefill throughput (prompt tok/s), decode throughput (generated tok/s), end-to-end latency (s/job, L+D=2048+128 canonical job); secondary columns = peak GPU memory during prefill vs decode, Wikitext-2 test PPL, C4 PPL (fixed seeded slice), and lm-eval zero/few-shot accuracies (ARC-c, ARC-e, BoolQ, HellaSwag, LAMBADA, OpenBookQA, PIQA, RTE, WinoGrande).
Aggregation: per condition report mean±std over n repeats; speedup ratio computed as ratio-of-means (mean(FP16)/mean(quant) for latency → <1 faster; mean(quant)/mean(FP16) for throughput → >1 faster), with a bootstrap 95% CI on each ratio (resample runs, n_boot=2000), never mean-of-ratios.
Paired statistics: because the same prompts/seeds drive all configs, use paired comparisons on per-run metrics vs C0 — Wilcoxon signed-rank (primary, non-parametric) plus paired t-test on log-transformed latencies as sensitivity; report p-values, effect sizes (Hedges' g), and treat significance as indicative given n=5.
Tradeoff verdict rule: compute precision deltas ΔPPL = PPL(quant) − PPL(FP16) and Δacc = acc(quant) − acc(FP16) with tolerance bands from the paper (approximately ΔPPL within ±0.1–0.3 and Δacc within ±1–2 pts for 4-bit). Verdicts: "pure speed boost" if C1 shows speedup within CI AND Δ stays inside bands while C2 (RTN) shows Δ clearly outside bands; "speed/accuracy tradeoff" if C1's Δ is material; otherwise quantify the magnitude. Report per phase (prefill vs decode) so the answer states, e.g., decode gains X× but prefill only Y×.
Sensitivity sub-experiment (budget permitting, on 7B only): calibration set RedPajama(canonical 512×2048) vs C4, and group size 128 vs 64, to bound calibration dependence.

(e) FEASIBILITY & RISKS
Estimated budget (1× H100): calibration ~0.5–1.5 h per model (512×2048 tokens); quantization minutes per model; inference grid ~ (3 sizes×4 configs×4 lengths×3 batches×5 repeats) — roughly 1–2 days per model at L2, dominated by 70B B≥8; Tier A (7B+13B) fits comfortably within ~2–3 GPU-days; Tier B (70B) adds ~1–2 GPU-days. These are design estimates to size the repetition/trim tradeoff.
Setup steps on target: install pinned torch/transformers/datasets/lm-eval-harness and vLLM (QuaRot fork); clone spcl-graph/QuaRot at fixed commit; build CUDA kernels via its Dockerfile; download gated LLaMa-2 checkpoints; quantize once per config and save checkpoints; run L1 and L2 benches; run quality evals with the same checkpoint.
Risks & mitigations:
  R1 Gated weights unavailable → blocker for the exact task; mitigation = pre-request HF access, mirror fallback; if unresolvable, the design stands but LLaMa-2 must be swapped (flag clearly, changes the answer).
  R2 Kernel build failure (CUDA/PyTorch mismatch) → pin repo CI versions; use repo's Docker image; do NOT fall back to FP16 fallback kernels (would invalidate W4A4).
  R3 QuaRot precision-mapping config ambiguity (INT4 weights vs FP8 activations/KV) → read and freeze the mapping from the pinned commit's config file and document it verbatim; all results referenced to that mapping.
  R4 Clock control unavailable → raise n, interleave, and report observed clock spread.
  R5 vLLM-fork divergence → rely on L2 phase-pure microbench as primary where L1/L2 disagree, and document both.
Artifacts: quantized checkpoints, raw timing logs + per-run values, aggregated tables, bootstrap CIs, and a results summary answering the question with a per-model speed/accuracy verdict and explicit phase split. Runbook scripts + requirements.lock committed for reproducibility.

STATEMENT: This is a design specification only; no experiment was executed, and no results are claimed.
